name: Roman Empire
modern_places: Italy; France; Spain; Portugal; Greece; Turkey; Egypt; England; Britain; Tunisia; Syria; Israel; Balkans; Mediterranean
territory: The Mediterranean basin: Western and Southern Europe, North Africa and the Near East
language_faith: Latin, with Greek in the east; traditional polytheism, then Christianity as state religion from 380
fact: Reached its greatest extent around 117 CE, roughly 5 million km², ringed by fortified frontiers.

name: Byzantine Empire
aliases: byzantium; eastern roman; eastern roman empire; byzantine
modern_places: Turkey; Greece; Bulgaria; Italy; Egypt; Syria; Balkans; Istanbul
territory: Southeastern Europe, Anatolia and the eastern Mediterranean
fact: Completed the domed Hagia Sophia in 537 and preserved classical Greek texts for a thousand years.

name: Ottoman Empire
modern_places: Turkey; Greece; Bulgaria; Serbia; Hungary; Egypt; Iraq; Syria; Saudi Arabia; Algeria; Libya; Balkans; Middle East; Istanbul
territory: Anatolia, the Balkans, the Middle East and North Africa
fact: Besieged Vienna in 1529 and again in 1683, and claimed the caliphate from 1517.

name: Mongol Empire
modern_places: Mongolia; China; Russia; Iran; Persia; Korea; Kazakhstan; Ukraine; Central Asia
territory: From Korea and China across Central Asia to Eastern Europe
language_faith: Mongolian; Tengrism, with wide religious tolerance
fact: The largest contiguous land empire in history, about 24 million km² at its peak.

name: Achaemenid Empire
modern_places: Iran; Persia; Iraq; Turkey; Egypt; Afghanistan; Pakistan; Syria; Israel; Central Asia
territory: The Iranian plateau, stretching from Egypt and Anatolia to the Indus
language_faith: Old Persian, Elamite and Aramaic; Zoroastrianism
fact: Built a 2,700 km Royal Road with relay stations, and let exiles held in Babylon return home.

name: Han dynasty
territory: China, reaching into Korea, Vietnam and the Tarim Basin
language_faith: Old Chinese; Confucianism as state ideology, plus Taoism
fact: Opened Silk Road trade with the west and produced the first known paper. China's largest ethnic group still carries its name.

name: Qin dynasty
territory: Northern and central China
fact: First to unify China. Standardized script, coins, weights and even cart axle widths; buried thousands of clay soldiers.

name: Tang dynasty
territory: China and Central Asia along the Silk Road
language_faith: Middle Chinese; Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism
fact: A golden age of Chinese poetry and early woodblock printing; its capital held around a million people.

name: Ming dynasty
territory: China
fact: Sent huge treasure fleets as far as East Africa, built the Forbidden City and rebuilt the Great Wall in brick.

name: Qing dynasty
territory: China, Mongolia, Tibet and Xinjiang
language_faith: Manchu, Chinese and Mongolian; Confucianism and Tibetan Buddhism
fact: Founded by a people from the northeast beyond the Great Wall; China's last imperial dynasty, weakened by the Opium Wars.

name: Maurya Empire
territory: Nearly the whole Indian subcontinent and parts of Afghanistan
fact: Its rock and pillar edicts preached non-violence; one pillar's lion capital is now India's national emblem.

name: Gupta Empire
territory: Northern and central India
fact: India's classical golden age: Aryabhata's astronomy, Kalidasa's plays and the place-value decimal system.

name: Mughal Empire
territory: Most of the Indian subcontinent
language_faith: Persian at court, later Urdu; Islam, with notable tolerance under one emperor
fact: Built the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort; around 1700 it produced nearly a quarter of world output.
capital: Agra, Fatehpur Sikri, Lahore and Delhi

name: Aztec Empire
territory: Central Mexico
language_faith: Nahuatl; Mexica religion centered on the sun and war god Huitzilopochtli
fact: Its island capital in a lake was fed by floating farm plots and held perhaps 200,000 people.

name: Inca Empire
modern_places: Peru; Ecuador; Bolivia; Chile; Argentina; Colombia
territory: The Andes of western South America
language_faith: Quechua; worship of the sun god Inti
fact: Ran a 40,000 km road network and kept records on knotted cords, without wheels or a written script.

name: Mali Empire
modern_places: Mali; Senegal; Guinea; Gambia; Mauritania; West Africa
territory: West Africa's Sahel, along the upper Niger River
language_faith: Manding languages; Islam blended with traditional beliefs
fact: Its ruler's 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca carried so much gold that prices in Cairo slumped for years.

name: Songhai Empire
territory: West Africa along the middle Niger River
fact: The largest state in West African history, broken by a Moroccan army with firearms at Tondibi.

name: Ghana Empire
territory: West African Sahel, in today's Mauritania and Mali
fact: Grew rich taxing the trans-Saharan trade of gold for salt; an Andalusian geographer described its court in 1068.
ruler: Kings of the Soninke Cissé dynasty

name: Kingdom of Aksum
aliases: aksum; axum; aksumite empire; axumite empire
territory: The Horn of Africa, across the Red Sea into southern Arabia
fact: Among the first states to adopt Christianity and to mint its own coins; known for giant carved granite stelae.

name: Carthage
modern_places: Tunisia; Libya; Algeria; Spain; Italy; Sicily
territory: North Africa (Tunisia), Sicily, Sardinia and southern Iberia
language_faith: Punic; Phoenician gods Baal Hammon and Tanit
fact: Its general crossed the Alps with war elephants in 218 BCE; its enemy later razed the city.

name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
aliases: assyria; assyrian; assyrian empire; neo assyrian
modern_places: Iraq; Syria; Turkey; Israel; Egypt; Iran; Mesopotamia
territory: Northern Mesopotamia, extending to the Levant and Egypt
language_faith: Akkadian and Aramaic; Mesopotamian religion led by the god Ashur
fact: A royal library of over 30,000 clay tablets preserved the Epic of Gilgamesh.

name: Akkadian Empire
territory: Mesopotamia (modern Iraq) and parts of Syria and Iran
fact: Often called the first empire. The founder's daughter Enheduanna is the earliest author known by name.
capital: Akkad (its site has never been found)

name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
aliases: babylon; babylonian; babylonian empire; chaldean empire; neo babylonian
territory: Mesopotamia and the Levant
language_faith: Akkadian and Aramaic; worship of Marduk
fact: Raised the blue-glazed Ishtar Gate and destroyed Jerusalem's First Temple in 587 BCE.

name: New Kingdom of Egypt
aliases: egypt; egyptian empire; new kingdom; egyptian new kingdom; ancient egypt
territory: The Nile valley, Nubia and the Levant
fact: One ruler briefly forced worship of a single sun disk; later kings were buried in a hidden valley of rock tombs.

name: Hittite Empire
territory: Anatolia and northern Syria
language_faith: Hittite, the oldest written Indo-European language; the 'thousand gods'
fact: Fought Egypt at Kadesh in 1274 BCE, then signed one of the earliest known peace treaties.

name: Umayyad Caliphate
modern_places: Syria; Spain; Portugal; Iraq; Iran; Egypt; Saudi Arabia; Morocco; Pakistan; Middle East
territory: From Iberia across North Africa and the Middle East to the Indus
fact: Built the Dome of the Rock and made Arabic the language of government across its lands.

name: Abbasid Caliphate
modern_places: Iraq; Iran; Syria; Egypt; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: The Middle East, North Africa and Persia
fact: Its House of Wisdom anchored the Islamic Golden Age; it ended when the Mongols sacked its capital.

name: Holy Roman Empire
modern_places: Germany; Austria; Czechia; Italy; Netherlands; Belgium; Switzerland
territory: Central Europe: the German lands, Bohemia, Austria and northern Italy
language_faith: German, Latin, Italian and Czech; Catholicism, later also Protestantism
fact: Its emperors were chosen by prince-electors; Voltaire joked it was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire.
capital: No fixed capital; Aachen, Prague and Vienna at different times

name: Carolingian Empire
modern_places: France; Germany; Italy; Netherlands; Belgium; Switzerland
territory: Western and Central Europe
fact: Its founder was crowned by the Pope on Christmas Day; his grandsons split it at Verdun in 843.

name: Khmer Empire
territory: Mainland Southeast Asia: Cambodia, Thailand, Laos and southern Vietnam
language_faith: Old Khmer and Sanskrit; Hinduism, then Buddhism
fact: Built the largest religious monument on Earth and vast reservoirs to water its rice fields.

name: Srivijaya
territory: Maritime Southeast Asia: Sumatra, Java and the Malay Peninsula
language_faith: Old Malay and Sanskrit; Mahayana Buddhism
fact: Controlled shipping through the Strait of Malacca; a Chinese monk stopped there in 671 to study Buddhism.

name: Majapahit
territory: Java and much of the Indonesian archipelago
fact: Its chief minister swore not to enjoy spices until the archipelago was united under one crown.

name: Russian Empire
modern_places: Russia; Ukraine; Finland; Poland; Kazakhstan; Georgia; Alaska; Central Asia
territory: Eastern Europe and Northern Asia, with Alaska until 1867
fact: Spanned three continents; its rulers abolished serfdom in 1861 and fell during World War I.

name: British Empire
modern_places: United Kingdom; Britain; England; India; Pakistan; Canada; Australia; New Zealand; South Africa; Egypt; Nigeria; Kenya; America; Ireland; Hong Kong
territory: Global, with holdings on every inhabited continent
fact: By the 1920s it governed about a quarter of the world's land and people, so the sun never set on it.

name: Spanish Empire
modern_places: Spain; Mexico; Peru; Philippines; Argentina; Colombia; Cuba; Chile; America
territory: The Americas, the Philippines and parts of Europe and Africa
fact: Silver from a single Andean mountain flooded world trade and helped make the first truly global currency.

name: Portuguese Empire
modern_places: Portugal; Brazil; Angola; Mozambique; India; Macau
territory: Coastal Africa, Brazil, India and East Asian trading posts
fact: First to sail around Africa to India (1498), and the last European power to hand back a colony in Asia.

name: Empire of Japan
territory: The Japanese islands, Korea, Taiwan and much of East Asia and the Pacific
fact: Turned a feudal society into an industrial power within a generation and defeated Russia in 1905.

name: Sasanian Empire
aliases: sasanian; sassanid; sassanian; sasanid; sassanid empire
territory: Iran, Mesopotamia and the Caucasus
fact: Captured a Roman emperor in battle in 260, and fell to the early Arab conquests.

name: Parthian Empire
territory: Iran and Mesopotamia
fact: Its horse archers shot backward while retreating, and they destroyed Crassus's legions at Carrhae in 53 BCE.

name: Seleucid Empire
territory: Syria, Mesopotamia and Iran
language_faith: Greek and Aramaic; Greek and local gods
fact: Formed from the largest share of Alexander's conquests; it got 500 war elephants in a treaty with an Indian king.
capital: Seleucia on the Tigris, then Antioch

name: Timurid Empire
modern_places: Uzbekistan; Iran; Persia; Afghanistan; Central Asia
territory: Central Asia, Iran and Afghanistan
language_faith: Persian and Chagatai Turkic; Sunni Islam
fact: The founder's grandson built one of the finest observatories of the medieval world.

name: Safavid Empire
territory: Iran, the Caucasus and parts of Iraq and Afghanistan
language_faith: Persian and Azerbaijani Turkic; Twelver Shia Islam
fact: Made Shia Islam Iran's state religion; its capital was praised as 'half the world'.

name: Ethiopian Empire
territory: The Ethiopian highlands of the Horn of Africa
language_faith: Ge'ez and Amharic; Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity
fact: Crushed an invading Italian army at Adwa in 1896, one of the few African states never colonized.

name: Kushan Empire
modern_places: India; Pakistan; Afghanistan; Uzbekistan; Tajikistan; Central Asia
territory: Central Asia, Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India
language_faith: Bactrian and Gandhari; Buddhism, Zoroastrianism and Hinduism
fact: Gandharan art fused Greek and Buddhist styles, and Buddhism traveled from here into China.

name: Chola Empire
territory: South India, Sri Lanka and coastal Southeast Asia
fact: Launched an overseas naval raid on Srivijaya in 1025 and built the towering temple at Thanjavur.

name: Vijayanagara Empire
territory: South India's Deccan plateau
fact: Portuguese visitors compared its capital to Rome; its army was shattered at Talikota in 1565.

name: Austria-Hungary
aliases: austro hungarian empire; austro hungary; austria hungary; dual monarchy; austrian empire
modern_places: Austria; Hungary; Czechia; Slovakia; Croatia; Bosnia; Slovenia; Poland; Ukraine; Romania
territory: Central and Eastern Europe
language_faith: German, Hungarian, Czech and a dozen more; mostly Catholicism
fact: A dual monarchy with two parliaments; its heir's assassination in Sarajevo set off World War I.

name: First French Empire
aliases: french empire; napoleonic empire; french; first empire
territory: Western and Central Europe
fact: Issued a civil code still at the root of many legal systems; dominated the continent until defeat in Belgium.

name: German Empire
aliases: second reich; imperial germany; germany; kaiserreich
territory: Central Europe, plus colonies in Africa and the Pacific
fact: Proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles; pioneered state pensions and health insurance.

name: Seljuk Empire
aliases: seljuk; seljuks; great seljuk empire; seljuq; great seljuq
modern_places: Iran; Persia; Turkey; Iraq; Turkmenistan; Central Asia
territory: Iran, Mesopotamia, Central Asia and Anatolia
language_faith: Persian and Oghuz Turkic; Sunni Islam
fact: Its victory at Manzikert in 1071 opened Anatolia to Turkic settlement and helped trigger the First Crusade.

name: Golden Horde
territory: The Pontic–Caspian steppe, from Ukraine to Kazakhstan
language_faith: Kipchak Turkic and Mongolian; Tengrism, then Islam
fact: Collected tribute from the Rus' principalities for more than two centuries.

name: Yuan dynasty
territory: China and Mongolia, with Korea as a vassal
language_faith: Mongolian and Chinese; Tibetan Buddhism with broad tolerance
fact: The first foreign dynasty to rule all of China, it issued paper money; Marco Polo claimed to serve its court.

name: Delhi Sultanate
territory: Northern India
fact: Turned back repeated Mongol invasions and raised the 73-metre Qutb Minar.

name: Kingdom of Nepal
aliases: nepal; gorkha; gorkha kingdom; kingdom of gorkha; shah dynasty
territory: The central Himalaya; at its peak it stretched from the Teesta River in the east to the Sutlej in the west
fact: Born from a hill state's conquest of the Kathmandu Valley; lost about a third of its land to the East India Company under the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, and became a republic by parliamentary vote.

name: Licchavi Kingdom
territory: The Kathmandu Valley and the surrounding hills
fact: Left Nepal's oldest dated inscription, carved on a pillar at the Changu Narayan temple in 464.

name: Malla dynasty
aliases: malla; mallas; malla kingdom; malla nepal
territory: The Kathmandu Valley, later split into three rival kingdoms
language_faith: Newar (Nepal Bhasa) and Sanskrit; Hinduism and Buddhism
fact: Split into three rival city-kingdoms whose palace squares are now World Heritage sites; the last fell in a single campaign of conquest.
capital: Bhaktapur, later also Kathmandu and Patan

name: Maratha Empire
territory: Much of the Indian subcontinent, from the Deccan plateau to Punjab at its height
fact: Its armies reached Attock and Peshawar in 1758, then suffered a crushing defeat at Panipat in 1761.

name: Sikh Empire
aliases: sikh; khalsa raj; sarkar-i-khalsa; punjab empire
territory: Punjab, Kashmir and the Khyber frontier
language_faith: Punjabi, with Persian at court; Sikhism, ruling Hindu and Muslim subjects
fact: Its ruler owned the Koh-i-Noor diamond; annexed by the British after two hard-fought wars.

name: Pala Empire
territory: Bengal and Bihar, at times much of northern India
language_faith: Sanskrit and early Bengali; Mahayana Buddhism
fact: Patron of the monastic universities of Nalanda and Vikramashila, which drew students from Tibet and Southeast Asia.

name: Tibetan Empire
modern_places: China; Tibet; Nepal; Bhutan; India; Central Asia; Himalaya
territory: The Tibetan plateau, reaching into Central Asia, western China and the Himalaya
fact: Briefly captured the Tang capital Chang'an in 763, and adapted an Indian script to write its language.

name: Song dynasty
territory: China proper; after 1127 only the south, below the Huai River
language_faith: Middle Chinese; Neo-Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism
fact: The first government to issue paper money and the first to use gunpowder weapons in war; finally conquered by the Mongols.

name: Goguryeo
territory: Northern Korea and Manchuria
fact: Repelled massive Chinese invasions by the Sui dynasty in 612; the name 'Korea' ultimately traces back to it.

name: Silla
aliases: shilla; unified silla; kingdom of silla
territory: Southeastern Korea, then most of the peninsula after 676
fact: Allied with Tang China to unify most of Korea; its capital's Cheomseongdae is one of East Asia's oldest surviving observatories.

name: Goryeo
territory: The Korean peninsula
fact: Printed the Jikji (1377), the oldest surviving book printed with metal movable type; the English name 'Korea' comes from it.

name: Joseon
aliases: chosun; choson; joseon dynasty; yi dynasty
territory: The Korean peninsula
language_faith: Korean, with Classical Chinese at court; Neo-Confucianism
fact: Its fourth king created the Hangul alphabet; it ended as the short-lived Korean Empire.

name: Tokugawa shogunate
aliases: tokugawa; edo shogunate; edo bakufu; tokugawa bakufu
territory: The Japanese islands
fact: Closed Japan to most foreign contact for over two centuries, admitting Dutch traders only to a small island in Nagasaki harbor.

name: Pagan Kingdom
aliases: pagan; bagan; pagan empire; bagan kingdom
territory: The Irrawaddy valley, uniting most of modern Myanmar
language_faith: Old Burmese and Pali; Theravada Buddhism
fact: Raised over 10,000 temples and stupas on one plain; more than 2,000 still stand.

name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
territory: Central Thailand, with sway over much of mainland Southeast Asia
fact: A cosmopolitan trading port built on an island in the Chao Phraya River; razed by a Burmese army in 1767.

name: Konbaung dynasty
aliases: konbaung; third burmese empire; alaungpaya dynasty
territory: Burma, at times Manipur and Assam
fact: Destroyed Ayutthaya in 1767, then lost three wars to the British; its last king was exiled to India.

name: Lý dynasty
aliases: ly; ly dynasty; dai viet; đại việt
territory: Northern Vietnam (the Red River delta)
language_faith: Vietnamese, with Classical Chinese in writing; Buddhism
fact: Moved its capital to Thăng Long (modern Hanoi) in 1010 and founded the Temple of Literature, Vietnam's first university.

name: Kingdom of Kush
territory: The Nile valley south of Egypt, in modern Sudan
language_faith: Meroitic and Egyptian; Egyptian and Nubian gods such as Amun and Apedemak
fact: Its kings ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty, and its royal cemeteries hold more pyramids than all of Egypt.

name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
territory: Egypt, with Cyrenaica, Cyprus and parts of the Levant
language_faith: Greek and Egyptian; Greek and Egyptian gods, including the hybrid Serapis
fact: Built the Library and the Lighthouse of Alexandria; its last ruler sided with Mark Antony and lost.

name: Kingdom of Zimbabwe
territory: The plateau between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers
fact: Raised massive stone walls without mortar; Chinese porcelain found there shows Indian Ocean trade. A modern country took its name.

name: Kingdom of Kongo
territory: The lower Congo River and northern Angola
language_faith: Kikongo, with Portuguese at court; Catholicism blended with traditional belief
fact: Its king became Catholic in 1491; his son later wrote to the king of Portugal protesting the slave trade.

name: Kingdom of Benin
aliases: benin kingdom; edo kingdom; benin empire
territory: The rainforest of what is now southern Nigeria
fact: Famed for brass plaques and heads that a British expedition looted in 1897; many are still held in museums abroad.

name: Oyo Empire
territory: Yorubaland and the savanna to the west, in modern Nigeria and Benin
language_faith: Yoruba; Yoruba religion, including the thunder god Shango
fact: Its cavalry forced the kingdom of Dahomey to pay tribute for most of a century; it broke apart after a revolt in its own provincial capital.

name: Ashanti Empire
aliases: ashanti; asante; asante empire; asante union
modern_places: Ghana; Ivory Coast; Togo; West Africa
territory: Central and southern Ghana
fact: United around a Golden Stool said to have descended from the sky; fought Britain in the War of the Golden Stool in 1900.

name: Zulu Kingdom
territory: Northeastern South Africa, between the Tugela and Pongola rivers
fact: Its army destroyed a British force at Isandlwana in 1879, one of the worst defeats of a modern army by an indigenous one.

name: Chimú Kingdom
aliases: chimu; chimor; kingdom of chimor; chimu empire
territory: The northern coast of Peru
fact: Its adobe capital was the largest city of pre-Columbian South America; conquered by a rising highland power.

name: Tiwanaku
territory: The Lake Titicaca basin, with colonies down to the Pacific coast
language_faith: Unknown, possibly Puquina; worship of a staff-holding creator god
fact: Built the Gateway of the Sun at nearly 3,850 m above sea level, one of the highest cities ever built.

name: Empire of Brazil
territory: Brazil, plus Uruguay until 1828
fact: The only lasting monarchy in the independent Americas; it abolished slavery in 1888, a year before the emperor was deposed.

name: Macedonian Empire
aliases: macedon; macedonia; alexander's empire; empire of alexander
modern_places: Greece; North Macedonia; Turkey; Egypt; Iran; Persia; Iraq; Afghanistan; Pakistan; Balkans
territory: From Greece and Egypt across the Persian lands to the Indus
fact: Conquered from Greece to the Indus in about a decade without losing a major battle, founding many cities named after its ruler.

name: Kievan Rus'
aliases: kievan rus; kyivan rus; rus; kiev rus
territory: The forests and rivers from the Baltic to the Black Sea
language_faith: Old East Slavic; Slavic paganism, then Orthodox Christianity
fact: Founded by Scandinavian Varangians; its prince's baptism in 988 brought Orthodox Christianity to the East Slavs. Destroyed by the Mongols.

name: First Bulgarian Empire
modern_places: Bulgaria; Romania; Serbia; North Macedonia; Greece; Balkans
territory: The eastern Balkans and the lower Danube
language_faith: Old Church Slavonic; Tengrism, then Orthodox Christianity
fact: The Cyrillic script took shape at its literary schools; a Byzantine emperor reportedly blinded 15,000 of its captured soldiers.

name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
aliases: poland; polish lithuanian commonwealth; commonwealth of two nations; rzeczpospolita; poland lithuania
modern_places: Poland; Lithuania; Belarus; Ukraine; Latvia; Russia
territory: One of Europe's largest states, from the Baltic almost to the Black Sea
language_faith: Polish, Latin and Ruthenian; Catholicism, with unusual religious tolerance
fact: Its nobles elected their kings, and a single deputy could veto parliament; partitioned out of existence by three neighbors.

name: Swedish Empire
modern_places: Sweden; Finland; Estonia; Latvia; Germany; Russia; Baltic
territory: The lands around the Baltic Sea
fact: Dominated the Baltic for a century; its huge warship Vasa sank on its maiden voyage in 1628.

name: Dutch Empire
aliases: netherlands; dutch; dutch colonial empire; dutch republic
modern_places: Netherlands; Indonesia; Suriname; South Africa; Sri Lanka; Taiwan; Brazil; America; Guyana; Caribbean
map_places: Netherlands; Indonesia; Suriname; South Africa; Sri Lanka; Taiwan; Guyana
territory: Trading posts and colonies from the East Indies to the Caribbean
fact: Its East India Company is often called the first publicly traded company; it gave up New Amsterdam, later New York, to England.

name: Rashidun Caliphate
modern_places: Saudi Arabia; Iraq; Iran; Persia; Syria; Egypt; Israel; Middle East
territory: Arabia, then Persia, the Levant and Egypt
fact: Conquered the Sasanian Empire and Byzantine Syria and Egypt in about twenty years; three of its four leaders were assassinated.

name: Fatimid Caliphate
modern_places: Egypt; Tunisia; Algeria; Libya; Syria; Israel; Sicily; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: North Africa, Egypt, the Levant and western Arabia
fact: Founded Cairo in 969 along with the Al-Azhar mosque, now one of the world's oldest working universities.

name: Ayyubid Sultanate
modern_places: Egypt; Syria; Yemen; Iraq; Israel; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: Egypt, Syria, Upper Mesopotamia, Yemen and western Arabia
fact: Its Kurdish founder retook Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187.

name: Mamluk Sultanate
modern_places: Egypt; Syria; Israel; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: Egypt, the Levant and the Hejaz
language_faith: Arabic, with Kipchak Turkic in the army; Sunni Islam
fact: Ruled by former slave-soldiers; stopped the Mongol advance at Ain Jalut in 1260.

name: Ghaznavid Empire
modern_places: Afghanistan; Iran; Persia; Pakistan; India; Central Asia
territory: Afghanistan, eastern Iran and the Punjab
fact: Its sultan raided India around 17 times; the poet Ferdowsi finished the Shahnameh in its time.

name: Tuʻi Tonga Empire
aliases: tui tonga; tu'i tonga; tonga; tongan empire
modern_places: Tonga; Samoa; Fiji; Wallis and Futuna; Niue; Polynesia; Pacific
territory: Tonga, with influence across Samoa, Fiji and other islands of western Polynesia
fact: Its sacred kings ruled from Tongatapu, where a later king raised the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui, a massive coral-stone trilithon.

name: Saudeleur dynasty
territory: The island of Pohnpei in Micronesia
language_faith: Pohnpeian; worship of the thunder god Nahnisohn Sahpw
fact: Ruled from nearly 100 artificial islets built of stacked basalt columns on a coral reef; overthrown by an invader from Kosrae.

name: Kingdom of Hawaii
aliases: hawaii; hawaiian kingdom; kingdom of hawai'i
modern_places: Hawaii; United States; America; Polynesia; Pacific
territory: The Hawaiian Islands
language_faith: Hawaiian and English; native religion, then Christianity
fact: Its last monarch was overthrown in 1893 by American businessmen backed by US Marines; annexed by the US in 1898.

name: Kingdom of Tahiti
territory: Tahiti and nearby islands of the Society Islands
language_faith: Tahitian; Christianity, adopted under the second king
fact: Became a French protectorate in 1842 and was annexed by France in 1880.

name: Kingdom of Fiji
territory: The Fiji Islands
fact: Lasted barely three years; amid debts and unrest, its king ceded the islands to Britain.
